¶ 59. Title. Mutability 1824, eds.
 even as] In the draft on p. 2 of Nbk 21 the line reads Brief although bright; S. carried this over to the
fair copy on p. 154 before substituting even as for although.
 how] too 1824, 1839, 1840, Rossetti 1870.
 Ironically altering the traditional sense of rich and poor in relation to the theme of Love — as
in Romeo and Juliet I i 212–13: ‘O, she is rich in beauty, only poor/That when she dies, with beauty
dies her store’.
 rich] rich is the reading of the draft in Nbk 21 front pastedown which S. transcribed into the fair
copy on p. 154, cancelled it in favour of proud written above the line, then underlined rich for reten-
tion. 1824 and eds prefer ‘proud’. The draft also shows the alternative line: [And leaves] despair.
 Virtue, Friendship, Love ‘outlive the joy which they briefly occasion, and the illusion of posses-
sion. Love flowers as bliss, but lingers as despair’ (Chernaik 156).
